Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A sharp-lapse-rate day with strong afternoon winds, high cloud cover at some sites, and isolated rain. Hallelujah stands out as favorable with a good evening ridge soaring window. Most other sites are marginal or unfavorable due to cross winds, hazardous low-level shear, or rain. Pilots must time flights carefully and watch for overdevelopment, shear, and icing.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — cross winds and high cloud cover; best window 1pm–3pm (peak w* 459 ft/min, ceiling 7107 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (10.1°C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — evening on-direction winds with good thermals; fly 4pm–7pm (peak w* 524 ft/min, ceiling 7833 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (10.2°C/km).
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — strong cross winds and hazardous low-level shear; if attempted, best 11am–1pm (peak w* 446 ft/min, ceiling 3635 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (8.4°C/km).
  • McClellan: Marginal — rain and low-level shear; window 10am–4pm offers lighter winds within preferred directions (peak w* 505 ft/min, ceiling up to 6317 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (9.9°C/km).
  • West McClellan: Marginal — rain and off-direction winds until late; window 4pm–6pm (peak w* 458 ft/min, ceiling 4255 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (9.9°C/km).
  • Peavine Mountain: Unfavorable — very strong winds (gusts 34 mph) and hazardous shear; brief window 11am–12pm (peak w* 477 ft/min, ceiling 4025 ft AGL) but winds still 15–17 mph. Sharp thermals (9.7°C/km).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal — hazardous shear and wind shifts cross after 12pm; fly 10am–12pm with light favorable winds (peak w* 559 ft/min, ceiling 7480 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (10.1°C/km).
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — low-level shear but flyable evening ridge soaring window 5pm–7pm with on-direction wind (peak w* 317 ft/min, ceiling 1894 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (10.0°C/km).
  • Daydreams: Marginal — weak thermals, hazardous shear, and strong afternoon winds; best 8am–10am (peak w* 192 ft/min, ceiling 2553 ft AGL). Sharp thermals (9.4°C/km).

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals region-wide (lapse rate 8.4–10.2°C/km) — advanced/expert pilots only.
  • Low-level speed shear ≥5 mph/layer at Slide Mountain (7 mph), McClellan (5 mph), Peavine Mountain (6 mph), Rainbow Ridge (6 mph), Duck Hill (6 mph), Daydreams (6 mph).
  • Thermal overdevelopment (clouds inside thermal zone) at Kingsbury, Hallelujah, Daydreams (27% of flying hours).
  • Rain at McClellan and West McClellan (regional peak 0.8 mm/hr).
  • Rotor/lee turbulence possible downwind of Peavine Mtn and Carson Range ridgelines with strong afternoon SW/W winds.
  • Icing risk above freezing level (~12,000–13,000 ft MSL) if climbing into clouds.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
